rationale: Create-from-template matches the revised materialize-by-slug spec, but Apply error and Cancel call setLoading(false) while template is still null, which mounts WorkflowForm and throws. Apply has no in-flight guard, slug changes can overlay a stale variables dialog, and tests do not lock seed yaml or the history-back Cancel path. Plan leftover-scan/raw_yaml mismatches were dismissed against the revised spec (18 dismissed, 0 deferred). Brief written to code-review-brief.md.

findings.title: Stale fetch can overlay popup
findings.problem: fetchData never aborts an in-flight GET and does not clear showPlaceholderPopup/pendingTemplateData at the start of a new run. A slower required_variables response for slug A can complete after slug B and reopen the variables dialog over the newer template.
findings.impact: The author can Apply values against the wrong slug, then save the wrong materialized YAML.
findings.recommendation: Abort the previous GET on slug change, and reset popup/pending/placeholders at the start of fetchData (and on the non-from-template branches) before awaiting.

findings.title: Error path mounts null WorkflowForm
findings.problem: handlePlaceholderSubmit catch and handlePlaceholderCancel call setLoading(false) while template is still null. {!loading && <WorkflowForm workflow={template} />} then mounts. WorkflowForm initializes guardrail_assignments from workflow.guardrail_assignments without optional chaining, so null throws. NewWorkflowPage.test.tsx mocks WorkflowForm to render nothing when !workflow, so the materialize-failure test still passes.
findings.impact: A live Apply error or Cancel unmounts the page with a runtime exception instead of keeping the dialog usable. A later successful Apply would also miss seed yaml because WorkflowForm does not resync from props unless templateKey changes.
findings.recommendation: Keep loading true while the variables popup is open, including after materialize errors. Render WorkflowForm only when template is non-null. Increment templateKey on successful materialize. Assert the real form (or an unmocked spy) is not mounted on failure.

findings.title: Cancel-back path is untested
findings.problem: handlePlaceholderCancel calls goBackWorkflows when history.stack.length > 1, which is the usual path from template details Create Workflow. NewWorkflowPage.test.tsx only exercises the empty-stack push to workflows-all and never expects goBackWorkflows.
findings.impact: Dropping or inverting the stack.length branch would send those users to the workflows list and the existing Cancel test would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Seed history.stack with more than one entry, click Cancel, and expect goBackWorkflows() rather than router.push({ name: 'workflows-all' }).

findings.title: Apply test misses seed yaml
findings.problem: The Apply-merge test GET yaml_config is 'states: []' and the materialize seed is 'states:\n  - id: start', but the assertion is only toHaveTextContent('states:'), which the pending GET yaml already satisfies. No other test observes seed yaml_config on the form.
findings.impact: If setTemplate dropped or failed to overlay seed.yaml_config, the author would save unsubstituted template YAML and CI would still be green.
findings.recommendation: Assert form-yaml equals the seed body (or contains 'id: start'), not a substring shared with the GET yaml.

findings.title: Apply has no in-flight guard
findings.problem: handleApply calls onSubmit(values) without awaiting or disabling the button. handlePlaceholderSubmit has no materializing flag and Cancel does not ignore an in-flight POST, so a late success can still setTemplate after the user has left.
findings.impact: Double Apply can fire duplicate materialize POSTs; fail-then-success races fight over popup/loading state, and Cancel can still apply a seed after navigate.
findings.recommendation: Disable Apply while materialize is in flight, await onSubmit, and ignore or abort the result after Cancel/unmount.
